title: Jura Server Guard malware_signatures entry
description: Schema for one entry of a jura-server-guard-incident file's `malware_signatures` array. See docs/SIGNATURE_IMPORT_FORMAT.md for the full authoring contract; this file is the machine-checkable companion, not a replacement for it. Validate with: python3 -m jsonschema -i your-signatures.json docs/schemas/signature-import.schema.json (wrap a bare array of entries as {"malware_signatures": [...]} first, or point this schema at one object at a time).

slug.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. This is the upsert key: re-importing a signature with the same slug updates it in place instead of creating a duplicate.

description.description: Optional free-text explanation shown in the panel and used as the default risk_explanation on a match.

type.description: Free-text finding type, e.g. webshell, structural, suspicious_php. Not an enum at the database level, but consistent naming keeps findings groupable.

pattern_json.description: Shape depends on pattern_type -- see the oneOf branches below and docs/SIGNATURE_IMPORT_FORMAT.md section 4.

target_extensions.description: Lowercase extensions without a leading dot, e.g. ["php","phtml","phar"]. Empty or omitted means every scanned file is a candidate -- the only scoping SignatureEngine::match() actually enforces before running pattern_json against a file.

target_paths.description: Stored and round-tripped for the panel/report, but NOT currently read by SignatureEngine's matching engine. Do not rely on this to scope a signature to specific paths -- use pattern_type: structural (path_regex/directory_names/path_contains) instead.

exclude_paths.description: Same caveat as target_paths: stored, not currently enforced by the matching engine.

required_hits.description: Stored and round-tripped, but NOT currently read by SignatureEngine's matching engine (a match is pass/fail per pattern_type's own rules, not a hit count against this threshold).

enabled.description: Ignored entirely when the import comes from the signatures feed (guard:feed-import) -- a feed-sourced signature always lands enabled=false with review_status=pending_feed_review regardless of this value, until an admin approves it.

source.description: Defaults to "incident:<incident.id>" (or "feed:<incident.id>" territory via the feed's own source field) when omitted. Set explicitly if a signature should be attributed differently.

substring.description: Legacy alias for `any`. Prefer `any` in newly authored signatures.

all.description: Every substring here must be present (case-insensitive) for the signature to match.

regex_all.description: Every regex here (PHP PCRE, with delimiters, e.g. "/eval\\s*\\(/i") must match.

any.description: At least one of these substrings (or of regex_any, if both given) must match, when either key is present.

not.description: If ANY of these substrings is present, the signature does not match -- a hard exclusion, not weighed against the other keys.

required_groups.description: Each group requires at least `min` hits across its own `any`/`regex_any` lists.

path_regex.description: PHP PCRE with delimiters, matched against the site-relative path.

directory_names.description: Matches when any of these appears as a whole path segment.

path_contains.description: Matches when any of these is a plain substring of the relative path.

require_path_and_content.description: When true, BOTH a path signal and a regex_any content match are required. Default (false/omitted): either alone is enough.

regex_any.description: Content-side regex(es); at least one must match the file's content.

same_directory_min_extension_variants.description: Multi-extension-spray detector: minimum number of sibling files (same stem, different extension) that must exist alongside this file. Requires filename_stem_pattern and extensions to also be set.

filename_stem_pattern.description: PHP PCRE (with delimiters) the file's basename-without-extension must match to be considered part of a spray, e.g. "/^[0-9]{5,}$/".

extensions.description: Candidate extensions checked for sibling files, e.g. ["php","PHP","phtml","pht"].
